What's new in 1.13:
• New 🧭 Portfolio Review (🔬 Stock Research menu): one click looks at all your stocks and open options and gives each a suggestion (Buy more, Hold, Reduce, Sell; Take profit, Let expire, Close, Roll...) with the reason
• A to-do list, most urgent first, with Done? ticks that are remembered
• Cash-secured put ideas for the stocks in your Stock Analysis: strike, expiry, premium, and a cash box that adds up what you'd use
• You can change any suggestion, and set your profit target and limits in ⚙
• 📊 Export to Excel saves the review in My Data → Portfolio Reviews
• Suggestions are rules-based ideas, not financial advice

history.notes:
What's new in 1.13:
• New 🧭 Portfolio Review (🔬 Stock Research menu): one click looks at all your stocks and open options and gives each a suggestion (Buy more, Hold, Reduce, Sell; Take profit, Let expire, Close, Roll...) with the reason
• A to-do list, most urgent first, with Done? ticks that are remembered
• Cash-secured put ideas for the stocks in your Stock Analysis: strike, expiry, premium, and a cash box that adds up what you'd use
• You can change any suggestion, and set your profit target and limits in ⚙
• 📊 Export to Excel saves the review in My Data → Portfolio Reviews
• Suggestions are rules-based ideas, not financial advice

What's new in 1.12.2:
• 📈 Stocks: the Call Premium column now counts every call you sold on a stock since the oldest shares you still hold. Calls sold before a later put assignment were left out before
• Stocks you bought yourself (not from an assigned put) now show their call premium too, once you hold 100 or more shares

What's new in 1.12.1:
• On 📋 Options, the box "Open Positions Net P&L" is now called "Premium Collected for Open Positions" (it always showed the premium on your open trades)
• Under it, two new lines from today's option prices: "Cost to close now" (what buying back everything would cost, with the $0.67 fee) and "If closed now" (what you would keep). Any option without a price yet is named, so the numbers add up
• The phone app's Home box shows the same

What's new in 1.12:
• Close or roll just some of a trade's contracts: the Close window has a new "Contracts to close" box. For example, roll 1 of 2 puts; the other stays open as its own trade (on the phone too)
• ✂ Split: the new ✂ button next to Close turns one trade into two, so each part can be rolled, closed or assigned on its own
• Saving no longer fails with "Access is denied" when OneDrive or another sync program is busy with your data file

What's new in 1.11:
• A tidier top bar: the buttons are grouped into drop-down menus (My Results, Find Trades, Stock Research, Data & Files, Settings). Import and Broker files are one button, and the new-high message is part of 🔄 Prices
• Stocks are shown one line per stock per account, with each purchase (lot) listed underneath: date, short or long term, cost and gain
• When you sell shares, choose which lots go: FIFO (oldest first), LIFO (newest first), Highest cost, or Pick lots by hand. Set your usual choice in ⚙ Settings → Selling shares
• 🏦 Broker files can bring in just your stocks (📈 Stocks only) and split them into dated lots from your Activity history
• No more Edge sign-in or extension pop-ups when OptionIQ opens
• Fixes "Update now" failing with "No such file or directory" on some new installs

What's new in 1.10.1:
• Fixes "Your change could not be saved" after OptionIQ sat open and unused for a while
• Mac: the desktop icon now starts OptionIQ (the first time, click Allow if the Mac asks about your Documents folder)

What's new in 1.10:
• 🏦 Broker files can now add an account that isn't in OptionIQ yet (➕ New account in the account lists)
• The Positions check can add open options that are missing from OptionIQ
• Assigned shares are no longer counted twice after a Positions check
• 🔄 Prices now runs by itself every 5 minutes (was 15) while OptionIQ is open in US market hours
• Opening OptionIQ again (for example from the desktop icon) while it is already running brings up the open window instead of starting a second copy
• Mac: OptionIQ closes itself a few seconds after you close its window, and the Terminal window closes on its own

What's new in 1.9:
• New 🎯 80%+ profit button on the Options tab: shows the open trades that have already captured most of their profit, so you can decide to close or roll. Change the % in ⚙ Filters (Profit captured ≥ %); it is remembered
• Bought options count too: their gain on what you paid
• While OptionIQ is open, 🔄 Prices runs by itself every 15 minutes during US market hours
• The phone app now shows each option's price next to what you sold it at (or paid), how much profit is captured, and a 🎯 list of the ones at your target

What's new in 1.8:
• New 🏦 Broker files button next to ⬆ Import: bring in your Fidelity Positions and Activity & Orders downloads. OptionIQ shows new trades, closes, stock buys and sells and reinvested dividends, and you choose what to add. Nothing is counted twice
• It also checks your share counts and cost per share against Fidelity and lets you tick the fixes you want
• 🌐 Get from Fidelity opens the Fidelity pages for you; download the files there and OptionIQ picks them up from your Downloads folder by itself
• You can pick several yearly Activity files at once
• New setup step and Settings card "Cost per share": reinvested dividend shares at $0 or at their price, and assigned put shares at the strike or at Fidelity's lower cost

What's new in 1.7:
• A small Week | Month switch above the boxes on 📋 Options: Month shows this month's net P&L, this month's premium and the average monthly net P&L. Your choice is remembered
• 📱 The phone app's Home screen now shows the same 8 boxes as the computer, with the same Week | Month switch

What's new in 1.6:
• 📱 Works with the new OptionIQ phone app: log, close, roll and fix trades and add watchlist stocks on your iPhone; OptionIQ adds them here within a minute or two (your data folder must be in OneDrive). A window lists each change as it comes in
• Close / Roll and ✏️ Edit now ask for the close price per share (for example 0.30), with no minus sign. OptionIQ works out the total with the $0.67 fee, just like a new trade
• Date boxes start on today's date
• The update notice shows only what's new since your version, with the buttons at the top

New in 1.5.1:
• 📊 Excel no longer stops with "Invalid count value" when a week had more options bought than sold
• Opening a second copy of OptionIQ (for example a test copy) no longer moves your desktop icon to that copy

New in 1.5:
• ＋ New Trade and ＋ New Holding now open in a pop-up window, so you can always see them, even when the page is scrolled down
• ✏️ Edit on a trade or holding also opens a pop-up with large boxes that show the current values

New in 1.4:
• ⬆ Import now works with your own spreadsheet layout. OptionIQ guesses which column is which, you fix any wrong guess from drop-down lists, and you see a preview before anything is saved
• Understands words like Put/Call, Sell/Buy, Sell to Open, Closed and Expired, picks the right sheet in an Excel file, and skips totals rows
• Clear Add and Replace buttons, and your column choices are remembered for next time

New in 1.3.2:
• New versions are offered as soon as you start the app
• Updates are much faster, show an "Updating OptionIQ" window and reopen the app by themselves

New in 1.3:
• Screener gives each trade a 0–100 Score and lists the best first (hover over the Score to see why)
• Weekly and Monthly quick settings in the Screener
• New 🔁 Roll candidates: shows roll choices for your open puts and calls, with your own settings for days, delta, in the money, and puts or calls
• Premiums shown after the $0.67 fee
• Warnings for upcoming dividends, too much in one sector, and price support levels
• The price message at the top can now be closed with ✕
